findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add _commands/completion_candidate.py to the step-4 inventory and route its sparse-checkout cone pattern (currently `set --skip-checks <ticket_id>`) through the layout helper so it demands <shard>/<id> for migrated stores and <id> for flat stores.
evidence: completion_candidate.py:111-116 runs sparse-checkout set '--skip-checks' <ticket_id> to demand a single ticket directory by its flat top-level name
The cone-mode sparse-checkout at line 107 plus the bare ticket_id pattern assume tickets live at the store root, not under a shard container
The step-4 inventory enumerates many _commands/*.py modules (claim/transition/txn/delete/compact*/fsck*/…) but does NOT list completion_candidate.py
Plan Scope: 'New code must read legacy flat and sharded stores during the expand phase' — a sparse-checkout that names only <ticket_id> resolves to nothing under the sharded path
findings.finding: The step-4 'Required inventory' omits _commands/completion_candidate.py, which composes a flat ticket path via `git sparse-checkout set --skip-checks <ticket_id>` and would materialize the wrong (or empty) tree under the sharded tickets/<shard>/<id> layout.
scenarios: Close-precheck / completion-verifier prepares an isolated candidate for a ticket that has been migrated into a shard; sparse-checkout materializes an empty tree and the verifier reads no events
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the store-relative cone path from ticket_layout (the shard relpath for sharded stores, the bare id for flat) and pass that to `git sparse-checkout set`, instead of the bare ticket_id.

findings.finding: Step 4's 'Required inventory' of tracker/<id> path-composition consumers omits at least three command modules that compose and reduce ticket dirs directly: _commands/transition_close.py, _commands/recent_creates.py, and _commands/_seam.py. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the crash/partial-move recovery contract: whether renames happen into git index/staging first (so an aborted run leaves the committed tree untouched) or how a re-run reconciles a worktree that already has some dirs moved but no migration commit.
evidence: 'precomputes all moves before mutation ... stages old+new paths, and commits one migration commit only when drift exists'
'holds the existing store write lock for one bounded local filesystem rename batch and one local git commit'
AC: 'a second run makes no commit' assumes a clean starting state; a crash mid-rename is not addressed
findings.finding: The migration performs an in-place rename batch under lock and commits only after all moves, but the plan does not state what happens if the process is killed AFTER some os.rename moves but BEFORE the single migration commit — leaving a dirty working tree with mixed flat/sharded dirs and no commit.
scenarios: Operator's migration process is SIGKILLed / machine loses power partway through the rename batch on the 6,008-ticket store
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step clarifying that renames occur against a working copy and are only made durable by the single commit (so an aborted run is discarded on the next checkout/reset), or that the re-run's move precomputation treats already-sharded dirs as no-ops.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the depth-aware shard-container recognition apply to the single `foreign_store_path_list` classifier in fsck_tracker_health.py (not just the report), so tracker-maintenance's deletion path also treats shard containers as store data.
evidence: Plan step 7: 'Make fsck/store-health depth-aware: valid shard containers are not FOREIGN_STORE_PATH, while unrelated top-level dirs still are.'
src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:111 foreign_store_path_list is 'THE single classifier for is this path store pollution? ... tracker-maintenance acts on it'

_holds_events (line 122) treats a top-level dir with no direct event file as non-ticket data; a shard container tickets/<hex>/ holds only ticket subdirs, not event files, so it would be listed as foreign
findings.finding: Step 7's depth-aware fsck change may not cover the single foreign-path classifier that tracker-maintenance uses to DELETE strays, so a valid shard container could be classified as FOREIGN_STORE_PATH and reaped.
scenarios: An operator runs `rebar fsck --repair` or tracker-maintenance against a migrated store; the shard containers are named as foreign paths and become deletion candidates.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend step 7 to state that the shard-container recognition is added inside `foreign_store_path_list` / `_holds_events` (the one classifier both the fsck report and tracker-maintenance deletion consume), e.g. a dir whose immediate children are recognized ticket dirs is store data, not a stray.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the post-rollback store state after a tickets-branch revert: confirm a reverted/older binary can still read the store (or document that the appended 'sharded-ticket-layout' capability makes it fail-closed) and how tickets written to shards after migration are recovered on rollback.
evidence: 'rollback is a tickets-branch revert or approved tracker-maintenance action, not an agent force/bypass'
'The migration appends that capability so older v1.0+ binaries fail closed on migrated stores'

In-place move migration (os.rename staging_dir -> ticket_dir under new layout) rewrites persisted record locations, triggering post-rollback-state applicability (records rewritten in place / read-path narrowed for old binaries)
findings.finding: The plan defines rollback as a 'tickets-branch revert or approved tracker-maintenance action' but never asserts the resulting post-rollback state — specifically whether the store remains correctly interpretable after revert. Because the migration appends the 'sharded-ticket-layout' capability so 'older v1.0+ binaries fail closed on migrated stores', a revert to a pre-migration binary would leave the store fail-closed / unreadable rather than merely carrying residual sharded dirs, and any tickets written to shards after migration would not be resolvable by the reverted flat-only reader.
scenarios: An operator migrates a store, new tickets land in shards, then reverts the tickets branch / rolls back to a pre-migration binary that fails closed on the stamped capability
A tickets-branch revert restores flat dirs but leaves post-migration shard-written tickets orphaned to a flat-only reader
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Deployment/Rollback assertion that a revert must restore both layout AND capability stamp, and either backfill-move sharded tickets back to flat before dropping the capability, or gate migration so no writes occur between migration and operator sign-off; add a heldout test that reads a rolled-back store with a pre-migration reader.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify or bound the single-batch/single-commit backfill for the 6,008-dir scale (expected lock-hold duration) or specify chunked/checkpointed batches, so the write-lock hold during migration has a stated bound.
evidence: 'holds the existing store write lock for one bounded local filesystem rename batch and one local git commit'
'The live 6,008-ticket cutover is still operator-scheduled so they can choose a maintenance window'
findings.finding: The migration executes the whole 6,008-dir backfill as one filesystem rename batch plus one git commit under the write lock, with no chunking/throttling or per-batch checkpoint; the plan bounds and defers live cutover but does not describe batched progress within the migration itself.
scenarios: Operator runs migration on the full 6,008-ticket store and the single lock-held rename+commit takes longer than expected, blocking all writers for the duration
